africaNews.title: Guinea sentences 224 people in illegal gold-mining crackdown
africaNews.summary: A court sentenced 22 former local officials and 202 miners over illegal mining and environmental offences in Siguiri; the crackdown has also triggered deadly clashes and displacement into Mali.
africaNews.content: The Associated Press reported that a court in Guinea sentenced 22 former local officials to two years in prison and 202 miners to three years over offences linked to illegal gold mining, environmental degradation and water pollution. The miners were also ordered to pay a combined fine of 10 billion Guinean francs. The defendants were among more than 1,200 people arrested in Siguiri, a major gold-producing area near the Malian border. The government says the crackdown is intended to prevent damage to farmland and rivers. AP reported that clashes during enforcement killed 10 people and injured 13, while tens of thousands of miners and family members fled towards Mali. Illegal mining supports livelihoods for large numbers of people, making enforcement and alternative employment central to the issue.

africaNews.whyItMatters: The crackdown brings environmental protection, public safety, cross-border migration and the livelihoods of mining communities into direct tension.
africaNews.whatHappensNext: Watch for environmental restoration measures, due process for those arrested and support for communities affected by the enforcement operation.

africaNews.title: Ethiopia and Sudan trade unverified accusations over support for armed groups
africaNews.category: Africa / Horn of Africa / Security / Diplomacy
africaNews.summary: Both governments accuse the other of helping armed opponents, but each denies the allegations and the Associated Press says it could not independently verify them.
africaNews.content: Sudan's military alleges that Ethiopia has allowed Sudanese paramilitary forces to establish camps and launch cross-border operations from its territory. Ethiopia, in turn, accuses Sudan of supporting Tigrayan rebels after fighting resumed in northern Ethiopia in September, undermining a 2022 peace agreement. Both governments deny the accusations. The Associated Press said it could not independently verify either side's claims. Sudan has raised its allegations with the United Nations and African Union, while Ethiopia expelled six Sudanese consulate staff and closed the mission. The tensions are unfolding alongside Sudan's devastating war and renewed instability in Tigray. Analysts warn that weapons, fighters and outside backers could turn domestic conflicts into a wider regional proxy confrontation.

nigeriaNews.title: Federal High Court rejects Atiku and ADC bid to amend Tinubu eligibility case
nigeriaNews.summary: Justice Inyang Ekwo refused the proposed amendments to Atiku Abubakar and the ADC's pre-election suit, but did not decide whether the NYSC discharge certificate at the centre of the case is genuine.
nigeriaNews.content: Atiku Abubakar and the African Democratic Congress brought their suit against President Bola Tinubu, the All Progressives Congress and INEC on 14 August. They allege that the APC submitted a forged National Youth Service Corps discharge certificate in support of Tinubu's nomination. Tinubu and the APC deny submitting a forged certificate and have asked the court to dismiss the case. On Friday, Justice Inyang Ekwo ruled that the original suit had been filed within the constitutional 14-day period, but that the proposed amendments would introduce fresh facts after the deadline. The judge therefore refused the amendment application and directed the parties to proceed on the original filings. This is a procedural ruling: it is not a finding that the certificate is forged, nor a final decision on Tinubu's eligibility.

nigeriaNews.title: Court orders ADC to restore Omar Suleiman as its Adamawa governorship candidate
nigeriaNews.summary: Justice Obiora Egwuatu ordered the ADC to submit Omar Suleiman's details to INEC after finding no valid basis for replacing the winner of the party's Adamawa primary with Tukur Ribadu.
nigeriaNews.content: The Federal High Court in Abuja ruled that the ADC must forward Omar Suleiman's details to INEC for publication as its Adamawa governorship candidate and directed the commission not to recognise or publish Tukur Ribadu as the party's candidate. The judge found no evidence that Ribadu had successfully challenged the primary result through a properly constituted party appeal process. The ADC and Ribadu argued that an appeal committee had reviewed the result and that the party's National Working Committee adopted its report; the judge rejected that explanation on the evidence before the court. Premium Times reported that Suleiman won the May primary with 143,216 votes, against Ribadu's 56,801. This Adamawa nomination dispute is separate from the appeal over the ADC's national leadership and Atiku's presidential ticket.

nigeriaNews.whyItMatters: The ruling tests whether party primaries and internal appeal procedures are applied consistently, and shows that different ADC legal disputes must not be conflated.

nigeriaNews.title: INEC says it will await Court of Appeal decision in ADC national leadership dispute
nigeriaNews.summary: INEC says it has been served notice of the appeal against the 5 November judgment that nullified the David Mark-led ADC leadership; the Nafiu Bala faction wants the commission to enforce the existing order immediately.
nigeriaNews.content: The 5 November Federal High Court judgment set aside the processes that produced the David Mark-led ADC national executive and invalidated decisions taken under that leadership, including Atiku Abubakar's nomination. The ADC says it has appealed and asked for a stay of execution. INEC National Commissioner Mohammed Haruna told PUNCH that the commission had been served notice of the appeal and would await the Court of Appeal's decision before determining its next steps. The rival faction led by Nafiu Bala Gombe argues that INEC should immediately comply with the subsisting Federal High Court orders and remove Mark and Rauf Aregbesola from its records. The competing positions remain part of an active legal dispute; the appeal has not been finally determined in the reports reviewed for this edition.

nigeriaNews.title: Opposition parties move national unity summit to 30 November
nigeriaNews.summary: The Coalition for Democracy postponed its second summit from 23 to 30 November so party leaders and presidential candidates can attend; no common opposition presidential candidate has been announced.
nigeriaNews.content: The Coalition for Democracy says its second summit will now take place on 30 November, after member parties requested a change because of campaign schedules. The coalition says it intends to sign a common agreement and set out a programme for democratic renewal ahead of the January 2027 elections. The parties named by the coalition include the ADC, Allied Peoples Movement, Nigeria Democratic Congress, Peoples Democratic Party, Peoples Redemption Party and Social Democratic Party. The proposed gathering is a step towards cooperation, not proof that the parties have settled their different presidential ambitions or agreed on a single candidate. The coalition says member parties will suspend campaign activities on the summit date to allow leaders to participate.

nigeriaNews.title: Peter Obi sets 10,000MW electricity target and makes health and education pledges
nigeriaNews.summary: At an Onitsha town hall, the NDC presidential candidate pledged 10,000MW of electricity, 10,000 primary healthcare centres and 40,000 primary-school blocks, without publishing a costed timetable in the report.
nigeriaNews.content: Peter Obi, the Nigeria Democratic Congress presidential candidate, used a visit to Onitsha to outline targets covering electricity, primary healthcare and basic education. He said an administration led by him would generate, transmit and distribute at least 10,000 megawatts of electricity, and also promised 10,000 primary healthcare centres and 40,000 primary-school blocks. He urged supporters to remain at polling units until votes are counted and results transmitted. The pledges are campaign commitments, not approved budgets or delivered projects. The reporting reviewed did not provide a financing plan, a phased construction timetable or staffing and maintenance costs for the proposed facilities. Voters will need measurable implementation details to compare the promises with other parties' programmes.

nigeriaNews.title: Police investigate alleged attack on NDC secretariat in Edo
nigeriaNews.summary: Edo Police say armed men allegedly damaged political materials at the NDC secretariat in Afuze; Owan East council chairman Ernest Aitalegbe was invited to assist the inquiry, not charged.
nigeriaNews.content: The Edo State Police Command says it has opened an investigation into an alleged attack on the National Democratic Congress secretariat in Afuze. Complainants told police that armed men wearing uniforms resembling those of the Edo State Security Network entered during a party meeting, damaged banners and other materials and threatened people present before leaving when police arrived. The allegations have not been established by an independent investigation. Police spokesperson Eno Ikoedem said Owan East Local Government chairman Ernest Aitalegbe had been invited in connection with the incident to assist investigators. The invitation does not establish that he knew about or participated in the alleged attack. The police commissioner warned politicians and supporters against intimidation and political violence.

nigeriaNews.title: Bayelsa boat tragedy: police report four deaths and 24 rescues
nigeriaNews.summary: Police say four people, including two children, died and 24 were rescued after a boat carrying mourners capsized in Southern Ijaw; the cause remains under investigation.
nigeriaNews.content: The Bayelsa State Police Command said a passenger boat travelling from Ayama to Ukubie for a burial ceremony capsized near the Oweikorogha–Otuan river junction in Southern Ijaw. Police reported that four people—two adults and two children—died and 24 passengers were rescued. Preliminary findings indicated that the boat developed a mechanical fault. Police said survivors were taken for treatment and that search and rescue work continued. The passenger count and full circumstances must be confirmed by the investigation; early accounts should not be treated as a final safety report. The tragedy renews questions about vessel maintenance, life-jacket use, passenger loading, operator training and enforcement on inland waterways.

nigeriaNews.title: Federal Government says annual medical-school admissions have risen to 12,000
nigeriaNews.summary: Education Minister Tunji Alausa says annual medical-school admissions have risen from about 5,000 to 12,000, with a target of more than 20,000 by the end of 2028.
nigeriaNews.content: Education Minister Tunji Alausa announced the figures at the inauguration of a 192-bed hostel at the College of Medicine, University of Ibadan. He said annual medical-school admissions had increased from about 5,000 before the current administration to around 12,000, with a target of more than 20,000 by the end of 2028. He also cited an increase in nursing admissions. The figures are ministerial statements and should be checked against enrolment and accreditation data from the relevant professional regulators. More places alone will not resolve workforce shortages: medical schools need qualified lecturers, laboratories, clinical placements, safe accommodation and sufficient funding. Retention, pay and working conditions will also influence whether trained professionals remain in Nigeria.

editorial.title: Nigeria's opposition must be tested by voters, protected by law and held to its promises
editorial.imageNote: No event photograph is needed for this original editorial.
editorial.summary: The latest ADC rulings are a reminder that democratic competition depends on both lawful party processes and independent courts. Procedural decisions must not be misreported as final findings, and opposition parties must answer questions about their own internal rules.
editorial.content: The court decisions affecting the ADC deserve careful, separate treatment. The refusal to amend Atiku Abubakar's eligibility case did not determine the authenticity of the NYSC certificate. The Adamawa judgment restoring Omar Suleiman concerns a different nomination dispute. The appeal over the Mark-led national leadership remains another proceeding. None should be collapsed into a single claim that the ADC has either been finally cleared or permanently removed from the 2027 contest. The ruling party and the opposition must accept lawful scrutiny. INEC must explain how it will apply court orders, publish clear procedures for election technology and protect equal access for parties and observers. Opposition leaders must also demonstrate that their own primaries, candidate substitutions and coalition agreements meet the law. Democracy is not strengthened by allegations alone; it is strengthened by evidence, due process, transparency and voters who can make an informed choice.

Atiku's separate eligibility suit against President Tinubu continues on its original filings after the court refused proposed amendments. In Adamawa, a different judgment ordered the party to restore Omar Suleiman as its governorship candidate. Meanwhile, the Coalition for Democracy has moved its summit to 30 November and lists the ADC, APM, NDC, PDP, PRP and SDP among its participants. A coalition can widen democratic choice, but only if its members publish clear rules, resolve internal disputes lawfully, agree on transparent candidate-selection procedures and present costed policies. The ruling APC should face scrutiny on its record, while opposition parties should face the same standard on governance, internal democracy and the credibility of their promises. Voters need a contest based on evidence and programmes, not simply personalities or accusations.

sportsNews.title: FIFA names Daniel Amokachi to NFF normalisation committee
sportsNews.summary: Former Super Eagles captain Daniel Amokachi is among five members named by FIFA to oversee the Nigeria Football Federation and prepare fresh elections, subject to eligibility checks.
sportsNews.content: FIFA has named a five-member Normalisation Committee to manage the affairs of the Nigeria Football Federation and oversee governance reforms ahead of fresh elections. The committee is chaired by lawyer Sampson Ebomhe and includes former Super Eagles captain Daniel Amokachi, sports administrator and journalist Godwin Enakhena, Amina Yerima and Dr Joe Abah. The appointments were communicated to the NFF on 18 November and are subject to eligibility screening by FIFA's Review Committee. The committee's mandate includes managing day-to-day affairs, reviewing NFF statutes and electoral rules, proposing reforms and organising fresh elections. FIFA says the mandate must end no later than 31 May 2027, and committee members are not eligible to contest the next NFF elections.
